Nullify

NUHL-uh-fy -- from Latin nullus ('none') + -ficare ('to make'). · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To nullify to make legally void or invalid.

A clerical error on the birth certificate was enough to nullify the entire passport application.

Worked Example

After discovering that one juror had lied about knowing the defendant, the judge has no choice but to throw out the entire verdict.

Making something legally void, as if it had never existed at all, is exactly what it means to nullify it.

How Nullify Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

revoke

revoke: to officially cancel or take back

invalidate

invalidate: to make invalid or legally void

Antonyms

ratify

ratify: to formally approve and make valid

uphold

uphold: to confirm or support a decision as valid

How Strong Is It? — revoke → invalidate → nullify

revoke vs. nullify

revoke vs. nullify: Revoke is often narrower than nullify -- you revoke a specific privilege, like a license or invitation, while nullify can wipe out an entire agreement, election, or law all at once.

invalidate vs. nullify

invalidate vs. nullify: Invalidate is very close in strength to nullify, both meaning to strip something of legal force, though nullify is the more classic word for courts undoing an entire law, contract, or election.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — null-

root — null-: none, nothing (Latin (nullus))

suffix — -ify

suffix — -ify: to make, cause to become (Latin (-ficare))

Put it together

Put it together: Nullify comes from Latin nullus ('none') plus -ficare ('to make') -- so to nullify something is literally to 'make it nothing,' stripping it of any legal force as though it had never existed.

Use the root in a new word: null

Use the root in a new word: null: Once the merger fell through, the original purchase agreement was considered null and had no further effect.

Word Choice

Nullify is most common in legal, political, and sports contexts -- courts nullify laws, referees nullify goals, and voters can nullify an election result through a formal challenge.
